what_it_does: This chip detects multiple different gases (hydrogen, ammonia, nitrogen dioxide, and others) simultaneously in wearables or tiny medical implants. It uses a stacked architecture: ultrasensitive membrane-based stress sensors sit on top of standard CMOS circuitry—the same electronics inside your phone. When gas molecules stick to each sensor's membrane, the membrane bends slightly; the chip measures this bend to identify the gas. Sixteen channels fit on a footprint smaller than a postage stamp and use only 1.47 milliwatts per channel, making it practical for battery-powered wearables.
